claims.statement: From 29 April 2025, updated ZUM rules require each submitted heating device to be registered in EPREL, signaling tighter documented product-quality purchasing in subsidized installations.
Installers and homeowners currently pay for commissioning, service callbacks, and evidence needed for eligible high-quality installations; actual callback losses are unknown.
A family-company operating relationship could support a consented pilot, but no customer files, equipment telemetry, or exclusive channel rights are currently granted.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Heat-pump installer owner or service manager
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Manufacturers provide commissioning apps; independent cross-brand callback analytics and installer proof packs are the wedge
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed installer contracts with homeowner consent
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Heat-pump installers and wholesalers, beginning with an arm's-length family-company pilot only if formally approved

fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Onboarding upfront and per-installation credits prepaid
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Assumption: 55-75% after sensors and remote specialist review
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Assumption: 1-2 hours remote review per installation plus installer field labor
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Electrical/HVAC scope review, device certification, GDPR, and professional liability
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Per commissioned system plus monitoring subscription
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Optional sensors, connectivity, telemetry storage, and specialist escalation

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Heat-pump OEMs expand native commissioning and remote diagnostics
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Current installer labor and travel for commissioning documentation, misconfiguration diagnosis, and avoidable callback visits
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Repeated callbacks, subsidy documentation requirements, or expansion across multiple equipment brands
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Each new installation and annual fleet monitoring

contrary_evidence: EPREL registration concerns product eligibility, not proof that commissioning defects are widespread.
OEM tools may already satisfy installers using one brand.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Proposed workflow-integration agreement for installer checklists and consented device telemetry; unsigned
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Sell a standalone commissioning checklist and uploaded-log review without integrations
critical_control_point.current_owner: Installers and homeowners control commissioning records and telemetry; manufacturers control device APIs
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed installer contracts with homeowner consent
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: The founder may request an arm's-length pilot through the family renewable business, but no data, staff time, customers, or rights are assumed
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Prospective business for QA scoring after consent; installer remains accountable for physical work
critical_control_point.subject: Installer commissioning record and consented telemetry workflow

economics.acquisition_route: Interview installers, measure callback cost, run 20 checklist-only commissions, then add telemetry for one brand
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Assumption: 20,000 annual commissions at 250 PLN plus monitoring produces over 5m PLN revenue; with 20% owner earnings and retained product equity, 5m PLN net worth is plausible in 6-10 years. Installation volume and savings proof are unknown.
economics.founder_time: 15-25 hours weekly; physical commissioning stays with licensed installers
economics.gross_margin_basis: Per-job and monitoring revenue less sensor, connectivity, specialist review, and support
economics.payback: Assumption: under 6 months if the product prevents one 800-1,500 PLN callback per several installations
economics.pricing: Assumption: 150-400 PLN per commission plus 20-50 PLN per system monthly monitoring
economics.retention_or_repeat: Repeated on every installation and through service life

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Cross-brand commissioning benchmarks tied to callbacks and seasonal performance
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Per-installation QA proof pack and remote monitoring
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Installer pays to reduce commissioning documentation labor and callbacks
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Subsidized-device purchasing now uses tighter product-registration rules

founder_fit: Family renewable-energy adjacency can enable a lawful test without assuming access.
Sensor analytics match the founder's data-science interests.
Installer-led fieldwork keeps the founder out of constant onsite service.
risks: Weak evidence that ZUM changes translate into QA demand.
Advice errors could affect heating performance and warranties.

structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: installer side proof and callback feedback loop
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: installer participation and device telemetry access

thesis: Tighter eligible-device purchasing can support a cross-brand commissioning proof layer if installers confirm callbacks are a costly unresolved loss.
title: Heat-Pump Commissioning QA Loop
uncertainties: Callback incidence and preventability are unknown.
Installer willingness to share outcomes is unknown.
Required certifications for remote recommendations are unknown.
